record.original_question: If a field F has cohomological dimension at most 2, is every central simple F-algebra a crossed product?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3. If F has cohomological dimension at most 2, is every central simple F-algebra a crossed product?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field. Recall that the cohomological dimension of $F$, denoted $\mathrm{cd}(F)$, is the supremum of integers $n$ such that there exists a torsion Galois module $M$ over $F$ with $H^n(\mathrm{Gal}(F^{\mathrm{sep}}/F), M) \neq 0$. A central simple $F$-algebra $A$ is said to be a crossed product if it contains a maximal subfield $K$ that is Galois over $F$; equivalently, $A \cong (K/F, G, c)$ for some finite Galois extension $K/F$ with Galois group $G = \mathrm{Gal}(K/F)$ of order $[A:F]^{1/2}$ and some 2-cocycle $c \in Z^2(G, K^\times)$.

Question: If $F$ is a field with $\mathrm{cd}(F) \le 2$, is every central simple $F$-algebra a crossed product?
artifact.category_tag: central simple algebras and Brauer group
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in published surveys of open problems on central simple algebras and is generally regarded as open. All known examples of non-crossed-product central simple algebras (going back to Amitsur) are constructed over fields whose cohomological dimension is at least 3, and no counterexample is known over fields of cohomological dimension at most 2; conversely, no general proof that every central simple algebra over such a field is a crossed product has been obtained.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on central simple algebras (Transformation Groups)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on central simple algebras, including the question of whether every central simple algebra over a field of cohomological dimension at most 2 is a crossed product.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is recorded as an open problem in a published survey on central simple algebras.

status_evidence.title: Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology (Cambridge)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference treating central simple algebras over fields of bounded cohomological dimension; no general crossed product theorem is given for cd ≤ 2.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references do not provide a resolution of the crossed product question for cd ≤ 2.
